detail: The story does not define the response body for an unknown item. Requiring an empty 404 body could reject a valid implementation that returns ProblemDetails. Put the unknown-item response contract under Open questions rather than enforcing this unspecified representation.

The story defines neither the valid ID range nor the status and ProblemDetails text for ID 0. Put these questions under Open questions until the story establishes the expected outcome; existing handler behavior alone does not make them acceptance requirements.

AC3 preserves other endpoints, but does not specify this endpoint's not-found status or response body. Keep these expectations solely as an open question unless the story explicitly adopts the existing error contract.

The story defines neither non-positive-id validation nor its exact status, content type and detail text. Keep these expectations solely as an open question until the story defines them; the implementation's declared result types do not establish the contract.

The case's layer is functional, with CatalogApiFixture as the precondition (the repo rule is xUnit v3 in tests/Catalog.FunctionalTests with Story/TestCase traits). The test is a Playwright APIRequestContext call against the running test stack, so it is not in the .NET functional suite and no trait filter can find it.

After step 2 the case expects the URL to contain type=7. The 'Filtered: <url>' caption appears in none of the keyframes (03, 04 and 05 show no caption), and the recording has no address bar, so ?type=7 is never visible. Only the active Navigation tag proves the filter. [raised by opus, sol]

The case expects 9 product cards. The '9 Navigation products' highlight frame shows only 2 full rows (6 named cards); the third row is cut off at the bottom edge, with only the SOLSTIX, B&R and QUESTER badges visible. The count of 9 and those three names are never in view. [raised by opus, sol]

The test asserts URL type=7, the active tag, the 9 cards and Category Navigation on /item/99, but the recording doesn't show it: the highlight keyframe meant to prove the final state (09) is fully white, and the captions set after the Navigation click ('Filtered: /?type=7 - 9 cards' and the three card-row captions) are missing from frames 03-08, while captions on other pages (frames 02 and 10) render. No frame shows the filtered URL. Wait for the filtered list to settle (11 products, tag active) before captioning, and for /item/99 to be stable before the final highlight, then re-record. [raised by opus, sol]

The case requires the response count to equal 101. The test subtracts additions and compensates for deletions made by another test class, allowing a different response count to pass. Establish the specified demo dataset and assert the actual count directly.

None of the supplied filtered-catalog frames visibly identifies /?type=7. The active Navigation tag and nine card names are shown across frames, but the URL caption supplied in code is absent from the recorded evidence. Preserve a readable caption containing the measured filtered URL.

The supplied frames never visibly identify the requested /item/1 URL or the alice identity. The sign-in highlight shows a generic account icon without an alice caption, and the product frames show tab-title and image measurements but omit the URL/as-alice caption. Capture readable evidence identifying this case's URL and user.
